items.finding: The review notes that temperature sensitivity of OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solutions in NIR and MIR, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: For a MIR ATR water measurement, this suggests sample temperature should be controlled or at least measured, and the first comparison should test whether temperature variation changes the spectra.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a review of biopharmaceutical downstream processing and refers to aqueous solutions, not a petroleum stream; it supports testing temperature effects but does not establish an in-line temperature-sensor design.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E02 ¶12

items.finding: In developing a robust model, the source varied temperature together with acid concentrations and ionic strength.
items.how_it_applies: This supports treating sample temperature as a variable to record and vary in a first comparison, so the assessment can see whether temperature affects the measurement enough to require an auxiliary temperature sensor.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The work concerns reactive liquid-liquid extraction in lithium recycling, not petroleum water determination; it is model-development evidence rather than an in-line temperature-sensor validation.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
citation.label: E01 ¶19
